subject: Urban Planning
title: Ankara: Moving a Capital to Build a Nation
description: A fast breakdown of Ankara: Moving a Capital to Build a Nation for builders.

hook.text: In 1923, Turkey's new republic needed a new capital. Istanbul was too tied to the Ottoman past.

buildup.text: Atatürk chose Ankara — a small inland town — and hired German planner Hermann Jansen to design it.

discovery.text: Wide European-style boulevards replaced narrow alleys. The plan signaled a break from Ottoman tradition.

twist.text: Ankara grew so fast it overwhelmed the plan. Squatter settlements surrounded the planned city core.

climax.text: Turkey's story repeats globally: planned capitals can't control the people who flock to them.

punchline.text: You can plan a capital. You can't plan who shows up.

quiz.question: Why did Turkey move its capital from Istanbul to Ankara?
options: Istanbul was damaged beyond repair in World War I
To symbolize a break from the Ottoman past
Ankara had better natural defenses against invasion
